Written 2026-10-18, before the old Mac is retired. Everything here lived only in

Plain language on purpose. Bart is not an engineer, does not work locally, and
checks the live site. No secrets or token values anywhere in this file.

## 1. The state of things right now

### Devotional email: fixed, and verified in production

This took three attempts and cost Bart two missed mornings. The final state is
working and confirmed.

**What it does now.** `public/devotional-schedule.json` is generated by every
build, alongside `knowledge.json`, and lists every published devotional
**including ones dated in the future**. The sender reads that file. There is no
longer a race where a devotional only becomes visible on its own day.

**Four send attempts a day**, at 06:20, 09:20, 13:20 and 17:20 UTC (1:20am,
4:20am, 8:20am and 12:20pm Central). One bad window heals itself by lunch. The
per-recipient ledger makes a repeat run safe.

**A health check at 18:20 UTC** (1:20pm Central), after every send window. It
counts who actually received the email, not whether the job claimed success, and
emails Bart only when a devotional was scheduled and nobody got it. Silence from
it means the devotional went out. That is deliberate: he said "I will have
connectivity, I just want to not have to be."

**Every run writes a row** to `ao_devotional_send_log`, including crashes.

**Verified 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-18**: the log shows four runs a day with
`source = schedule`, and October 17 was sent by `daily_cron`, the first time the
Vercel cron has ever actually delivered the email.

## 2. Decisions made, and why

**Posting cadence, set by Bart on 2026-10-04.** Quote cards every three
**working** days, weekends skipped. Reshares on Monday, Wednesday and Friday
only. Both are enforced in `lib/ao/postingCadence.js` rather than left to
whatever the engagement numbers prefer, because a cadence he decided on was
drifting week to week.

**Reshares are published to five channels by default.** Previously the reshare
and quote card flows named only four accounts and silently left his personal
Instagram out, which is why that account received journal entries and no quote
cards for months. It looked like a broken channel and was actually a channel
nothing was ever addressed to.

**Journal entries are not re-dated to rotate them back to the top of the site.**
The publish date is the key the email system dedupes on. Changing it would make
the system see a post it has never sent for that date and email 175 people a
piece from July. If resurfacing is wanted, build a "worth revisiting" section
that reads from the reshare queue, and leave the dates alone.

**The engagement inquiry form now asks who is filling it in.** It never did.
Every engagement inquiry before 2026-10-04 arrived anonymous unless the sender
happened to name themselves inside an answer, and nothing was stored anywhere, so
the notification email was the only copy. Name and email are now required, phone
optional, and **every submission is written to `engagement_inquiries` before the
email is sent**, so a failed notification is no longer a lost person.

**LinkedIn data deletion was built because the honest answer was no.** Nothing
was being hoarded; nobody had written the function, and "no" to that question
ends the application. It is a screen at `/api/ao/linkedin-data` rather than a
script, so it can be shown working on camera.

**The application obtains no LinkedIn member identities, and that is a position
worth stating rather than a gap.** It reads two integers off `socialActions` and
never calls the sub-resources that return who reacted or commented. A test fails
if any LinkedIn code starts requesting them.

**Archetype Original has one member, permanently.** Bart's own words: "I am the
only and will be the only member for the indefinite future. This app is merely
for me to publish the content I write with Auto." That single fact answers two
of LinkedIn's four questions outright and is written up as the frame for all
four.

### Secrets, and what nobody has

`CRON_SECRET` is set on Vercel production **and** as a GitHub Actions secret.
They match. **Nobody holds the value**, including Bart, because it was generated
inline and never written down.

Consequence: **cron endpoints cannot be triggered by hand any more.** To recover
a missed devotional, run the `update-journal.yml` workflow from GitHub, which
carries the secret. If manual triggering is ever needed often, build an
owner-session-authenticated "run now" button instead of sharing the secret.

## 4. Traps, learned the hard way

**A green deploy is not a working feature.** On 2026-10-04 a devotional fix was
reported as shipped on the strength of a deploy going green. It had never worked
in production. The files it needed were not bundled into the serverless function,
so it silently fell back to the old path every morning for two days. **Verify by
reading what the thing actually did**, not by watching it deploy.

**A `200 OK` that did nothing is the most dangerous response in this codebase.**
The weekly pull-quote job answered "all good" every Monday for months while
building nothing, because a setting it needed was never filled in. The devotional
sender answered "no devotionals published today" on days one was published.
Prefer a loud failure to a quiet success.

**Record before you send, not after.** The devotional send marked the day handled
before the emails went out, so "claimed" and "delivered" were different
questions. The broadcast also reported delivered addresses only after the whole
list finished, so a crash partway through would have re-emailed everyone. Both
now record as they go.

**`node --check` and a full test suite will not catch an out-of-scope variable.**
A `const` was moved inside a branch while three later lines still used it. Valid
syntax, 1,334 tests green, build green, deploy green, and the function threw
`ReferenceError` in production every morning for ten days. **eslint with
`no-undef` is now wired into the build** (`npm run verify:scope`) and was proven
against that exact bug.

**This repo has guards. Respect them, they are right.**
`verify-no-direct-table-access` blocks direct access to `ao_scheduled_posts` and
caught a shortcut before it shipped. `verify-voice` catches em dashes.
`verify-vercel-config` checks the builds. Two of the worst mistakes this month
were caught by checks already in the codebase.

**Every API endpoint needs a `routes` entry in `vercel.json`.** This project uses
the legacy `builds` and `routes` configuration. An unrouted endpoint returns the
single page app's HTML with a `200`, which looks like success and is not.

**`includeFiles` matters, and a missing one is invisible.** A serverless function
cannot read repository files unless they are listed. A directory of 302 markdown
files did not travel; one small generated JSON file next to `knowledge.json`
does, because that path was already proven.

**GitHub scheduled workflows run four to six times a day, not hourly**, whatever
the cron expression says. Anything that must happen daily cannot depend on one of
them landing in a particular window.

**Locking a door means checking who was already walking through it.** Setting
`CRON_SECRET` on 2026-10-02 immediately broke the devotional sender, which had
been calling in without one for months. Bart lost a day's email to that.

**Artifacts cannot load images from another website.** They fail silently, with
no broken image icon. Ship images as files alongside the page.

**Never re-date a journal entry.** See section 2.

## 6. One thing that is not a task

An engagement inquiry arrived on 2026-10-04 from someone referring to a
conversation Bart had with them in the spring. It carried **no name, no email,
no phone**, because the form had never asked and nothing was stored. It is
unrecoverable. The sender described themselves as an Operations Coordinator at a
150-plus person organization who works behind the scenes and wants to share their
story as motivation for people who are struggling.

They said twice that they were not sure their story counted as leadership. They
reached out anyway.

If Bart works out who it is, a mentor session or a podcast conversation is
probably the right door, not an engagement.
